title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, as reconstructed from pp. 42–44. S is a set with a topology τ. T ⊂ S is τ-closed, with complement U = S∖T. On T we are given a topology τ'_0 finer than τ|T. Let C be the class of topologies τ'' on S such that:
- τ'' is finer than τ;
- τ'' induces τ'_0 on T;
- τ'' induces τ|U on U.

The margin adds the case 'T closed in S'. Since τ'' is finer than τ, T is automatically τ''-closed.

The topology τ' is defined by its closed sets: X is τ'-closed iff X = B ∪ cl_τ(X∩U), with B ⊂ T closed for τ'_0. The previous page shows this is a family of closed sets: stable under arbitrary intersections and finite unions.

This page proves the following.
- τ' is finer than τ. If X is τ-closed, then X∩T is τ|T-closed, hence τ'_0-closed, and X = (X∩T) ∪ cl_τ(X∩U).
- τ' induces τ'_0 on T. For X ⊂ T we have X∩U = ∅, so X = B.
- Hence τ' ∈ C. (That τ'|U = τ|U was the 'last assertion already proved'.)
- τ' is the coarsest member of C. Take τ'' ∈ C. B is τ'_0 = τ''|T-closed and T is τ''-closed, so B is τ''-closed in S. Also cl_τ(X∩U) is τ-closed, hence τ''-closed, so their union X is τ''-closed. This proves a), b), c).
- Part d) begins: compare the specialization preorders, where x ≤ y iff x ∈ cl({y}).
  - Pairs inside T or inside U are clear, since τ'|T = τ'_0 and τ'|U = τ|U.
  - x ∈ U, y ∈ T cannot occur, because cl_τ'(y) ⊂ T as T is τ'-closed.
  - x ∈ T, y ∈ U: the claim is x ≤_τ' y iff x ≤_τ y. This reduces (p. 44) to cl_τ'(Y) = cl_τ(Y) for Y ⊂ U. That holds because any τ'-closed X containing Y contains cl_τ(X∩U) ⊇ cl_τ(Y).

Purpose. This is a lemma for the 'algèbre des figures'. One refines the topology on a closed stratum T, keeps the open part U, and takes the coarsest compatible topology on S. It feeds into e) on p. 44 and the construction on p. 42. There, I is obtained from I' and J, with the topology of I final/quotient for I' → I and J → I, which excludes the trivial sum topology J ⊔ U.
errors: No mathematical error found. One hypothesis is used implicitly: membership in C is taken to imply that T is closed for τ''. This is automatic because τ'' is finer than τ and T is τ-closed; the left-margin note seems to record exactly this.
Two points are not proved on this page but on neighbouring pages: that the family is stable under intersections and finite unions (p. 42), and that τ'|U = τ|U (described as 'already proved').

ideas.what: Coarsest topology on S that refines τ, restricts to a prescribed finer topology on a closed subset T, and is unchanged on U = S∖T. Closed sets are B ∪ cl_τ(X∩U).
ideas.modern_name: Coarsest refinement of a topology along a closed subspace (modification of a topology on a closed stratum; a gluing/attaching-type topology)

ideas.what: Closures of subsets of the open part U are unchanged by the refinement. Hence the specialization preorder for points of T versus points of U is unchanged, and no point of U specializes into... rather, no point of U lies in the closure of a point of T.
ideas.modern_name: Specialization order / closure comparison under refinement

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but elementary general-topology lemma (coarsest refinement along a closed subset, with closures preserved on the open part). It serves Grothendieck's 1986 'algèbre des figures' construction. Nothing here would surprise a specialist or appear to be missing from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the topology is likely 'plus fine que τ' (the original topology), not τ'. The claim proved is that τ' is finer than τ.

'on va voir [?] W [?] que' probably reads 'on va voir d'abord que' or similar. W seems to be a reading artefact; the same applies to the 'W' in the bottom margin note, possibly 'NB c'est vrai dans tous les cas où x∈T'.
Left margin likely reads '(cas des topologies plus fines pour lesquelles T fermé dans S)'.
